newsitem.title: USA: Another Fidelity fund manager leaves.
newsitem.headline: Another Fidelity fund manager leaves.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said Friday a veteran fixed-income mutual fund manager has decided to leave the company, a week after two other managers announced they would quit to join smaller firms.
Fund manager Michael Gray, who managed or co-managed nine different mutual funds, has decided to leave the massive mutual fund company to start his own investment management firm, Fidelity said.
"He's going to take some time off and then he's going to start his own investment management firm specialising in fixed income," Fidelity spokeswoman Teri Kilduff said.
"Michael has done a fine job for shareholders. We are sorry to see him leave but we respect his decision," she said.
Kilduff said Fidelity would name replacements for Gray at a later date.
Gray managed the fixed-income portions of the $11.2 billion Asset Manager fund, the $3.4 billion Asset Manager: Growth fund, and the $589 million Asset Manager: Income fund.
A 14-year veteran with the company, he also managed the fixed-income assets of the $4.1 billion Balanced fund and he co-managed three of Fidelity's VIP funds.
David O'Leary, president of Alpha Equity Research, said he estimates that Gray was responsible for around $10 billion in assets at the nine funds.
Gray's exit follow's last week's news that fund managers Larry Greenberg and Andrew Offit were also quitting.
